activity.role: Vice-President of the Council of Ministers under Paul Reynaud
activity.notes: Appointed Vice-President of Council and Minister of State on 18 May 1940, continued until 16 June formation of his own cabinet. Same-day transition boundary reflects new government formation; not a separate state. Activity domain emphasis: governance.

sources.title: Larousse — Philippe Pétain, Encyclopédie
sources.citation_text: Larousse documents his war ministry Feb 1934, Bouisson state ministry June 1935, Franco embassy and Reynaud vice premiership on 18 May 1940.

sources.title: Archontology — Henri-Philippe-Bénoni-Omer-Joseph Pétain
sources.citation_text: Individual office chronology: minister of war 9 Feb–8 Nov 1934, 1–4 June 1935 minister of state, deputy PM 18 May–16 June, PM from 16 June 1940 until 18 April 1942, de facto state head 11 Jul 1940–20 Aug 1944.
